subject: FinTechCo - multi-region perf follow-up + competitive comparisons
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechCo - multi-region perf follow-up + competitive comparisons

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

Summary of discovery:
- Primary use: low-latency inference for transaction scoring across US/EU customers; strong demand in APAC for reporting (not real-time yet).
- Current pain: inconsistent geo latency from current provider (vendor X on AWS in us-west), limited region availability, and lack of clear fallback when capacity spikes.
- Security: SOC 2 + regional data residency for EU production data is mandatory.

Redwood takeaways / differentiators (high level):
- Unified API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments so you can start hosted and move to Dedicated or VPC as needs grow.
- Smart routing + regional fallbacks: requests can be routed by latency and cost policy; will fail over to a region-compatible variant when needed.
- KV/prefix caching and continuous batching to reduce p95/p99 token latency for repeated patterns (helps transaction scoring).
- Transparent perf profiles for our curated model catalog — we can share region-by-region p50/p95 numbers and run a FinTechCo-focused test.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm the regions you want in the test (I suggest us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1).
2) Share preferred test window (we can run synthetic and live traffic replay).
3) We’ll provide: a short runbook + a shared perf dashboard (link below), and a competitive sheet comparing Redwood vs Bedrock/GCP Vertex for the same model family.

Attachments: redwood-multi-region-latency.pdf (summary), redwood-competitive-diff.docx (high level).
Shared dashboard: https://redwood.app/shared/perf-dashboard/fintechco

If you confirm regions and a 2–4 hour window next week, we’ll schedule the tests and loop in infra for any whitelisting.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

From: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - multi-region perf follow-up + competitive comparisons

Hey Jordan —

Thanks for the recap — that covers it. A few clarifications and asks from our side before we lock in a window:

1) Regions: yes to your suggestion (us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1). For EU production data we need to ensure data residency (no egress to US). Can you confirm the deployment option that supports EU-only residency and what the timeline looks like to enable that?

2) Competitive numbers: our infra lead (Mark) wants a side-by-side p50/p95 for cold and warm starts vs:
   - Current provider (Vendor X on AWS us-west/us-east),
   - AWS Bedrock (same model family),
   - GCP Vertex AI endpoints
Please include details on test methodology (concurrency, payload sizes, tokenization).

3) Security: link to SOC 2 evidence and typical audit time if we request SOC-related artifacts.

4) Test window: next Tue/Wed morning (US East) works for our team — prefer a 2–3 hour block.

If you can get the sample numbers and the runbook today/tomorrow, we’ll confirm a slot.

—Asha
Asha Iyer
Head of Platform Engineering
FinTechCo
asha.iyer@fintechco.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - multi-region perf follow-up + competitive comparisons

Asha —

Great, thanks — confirmed regions and preference for Tue/Wed next week. Attached is a short runbook (runbook-multi-region-tests.md) and the high-level competitive sheet (redwood-competitive-diff.docx). We’ll publish the detailed methodology to the shared dashboard before the run:

Planned tests (high level):
- Cold-start latency: single-request p50/p95 across regions (model: vicuna-13b-equivalent quantized), payload sizes: 64/256 tokens.
- Warm steady-state: 20 RPS sustained for 10 minutes, measure p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
- Live replay: up to 100 RPS injected from your replay (if you provide), measure tail latency and throughput.

Competitive comparators and methodology notes:
- We will run the same model family compiled for each provider where possible (same tokenization & prompt).
- For Bedrock/Vertex we run standard managed endpoints; for Vendor X we’ll use a comparable config where they expose it.
- All tests run from our runner in the region (no cross-region proxies) to capture true region-to-inference latency.

Redwood-specific notes that matter to p95/p99:
- KV caching: repeated prefixes (common in scoring) will see large tail reductions. We’ll include both with/without cache runs.
- Smart routing: if a region sees high queuing we can transparently route to a pinned near-region variant — we’ll include a simulated spike test to show graceful degradation.

Attachments: runbook-multi-region-tests.md, redwood-competitive-diff.docx.
Dashboard (will be live before tests): https://redwood.app/shared/perf-dashboard/fintechco
SOC 2 evidence: we’ll share our SOC 2 Type II report via secure link — timeline ~48 hours for read-only access request.

Marissa/Sean — can you take point on running the Bedrock/Vertex comparators and capture artifact links? I’ll coordinate with infra for any IP allowlist.

Thanks —
Jordan
